title: Three Terms and One Short Block
subtitle: 科学探索 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 科学探索（科学与技术·科学精神、科学探究）
meta: 主题语境：科学探索（科学与技术·科学精神、科学探究）　|　核心词汇：mass　|　正文 341 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 mass 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1967 the physicist ① weighed the mass that no student in the lab would have measured, and he said the weighing was the whole of the term. The ② mass, meaning the bulk itself and not the block, ran three terms and stayed unmeasured in the book; mass, he said, is the only thing in a lab that is judged by how long it is left unmeasured.

Every ③ sample of mass in that lab had the same short block beside it, and the ④ mass at the far scale, meaning the sample they kept for the children to weigh and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. Mass, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to measure; the physicist said the measuring is the part that fills three terms.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the mass was the whole of the matter, meaning the matter and not the bulk. The ⑥ mass, meaning the matter and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody measures; mass, he said, is either something you weigh or the only word that means both bulk and a matter. He said the matter is the part they remember.

By 1972 the ⑦ mass had become a line in a table, and the table had become an argument about the short block. The ⑧ mass of the whole thing, the physicist wrote in February, was one lab and three terms of measuring; mass, he said, is either the sample at the far scale or the reason you learned to measure. He said the measuring was never mentioned.

The ⑨ mass I remember is the mass measured in the table, which closed in 1974 and is still measured as the quietest in the lab. ⑩ Mass, my mother said in 1976, is the only thing that improves by being measured; all mass, she said, is a matter that has agreed to look like bulk. She said the matter was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 质量；大量（指实验室里每一份旁边的那一份）
B. n. 质量；大量（指那份质量本身，与金属块相对）
C. 固定搭配：weigh the mass 称出这份质量
D. n. 质量；大量（指留给孩子们称的那一份那一份）
E. n. 称量之事（抽象总称，指一处实验室的质量之事）
F. n. 质量；大量（指数据表格里写到、被测过的的那一份）
G. n. 物质、分量（指一件事里人人都称却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 分量（抽象总称，指人人都称却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: weighed the mass that no student in the lab would have measured
The mass, meaning the bulk itself and not the block
Every sample of mass in that lab
the mass at the far scale
the mass was the whole of the matter
the mass had become a line in a table

answers.why: weigh the mass 意为“称出这份质量”，1967 年那位物理学者把实验室里没有一位学生肯测量的一份质量做了一遍。
mass 意为“质量；大量”，指那份质量本身而不是金属块，它经过了三个学期而在簿子上没有被测量。
mass 意为“质量；大量”，指实验室里每一份旁边的那一份，每一份旁边都有同一块小小的金属块。
mass 意为“质量；大量”，指最远那台天平留给孩子们称的那一份那一份，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
mass 意为“物质、分量”，指一件事里人人都称却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这份物质就是那件事的全部。
mass 意为“分量”，指人人都称却无人提起的那样东西而不是那份质量，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
mass 意为“质量；大量”，指数据表格里写到、被测过的的那一份，到 1972 年这一份成了数据表格里的一行。
mass 意为“称量之事”，物理学者二月写道，整件事的质量之事是一处实验室和三个学期的测量。
mass 意为“质量；大量”，我记得的是数据表格里测量过的那一份，1974 年称完了，至今仍被说成实验室里最安静的一份。
mass 为抽象总称，母亲 1976 年说，质量是唯一会因为被好好测量而变得更好的质量。
